speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've experienced any headache, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light over the last two days? Also, have you had any recent travel or mosquito bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are taking haloperidol; when did you last take a dose, and have you noticed any muscle stiffness or rigidity along with your fever? Given your altered mentation and medication history, I need to rule out a drug reaction immediately. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Creatine Kinase.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: White Blood Cell Count: 14,700/mm³ (elevated), Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated). Comprehensive Metabolic Panel data not provided in current records.

speaker: Doctor
text: The extremely high Creatine Kinase and fever while on haloperidol strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, but I need to confirm your physical status. Do you have any muscle rigidity, sweating, or blood pressure instability right now? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Liver Function Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine Toxicology: Negative. Liver Function Tests: Data not provided. Additional findings from Vital Signs: Temperature 39.6°C (103.2°F), Heart Rate 116/min. Neurological Examination: Generalized rigidity, Mental Status Confused and disoriented. Lumbar Puncture: CSF Opening Pressure 22 cm H2O, CSF White Blood Cells 4 cells/mm3, CSF Red Blood Cells 0 cells/mm3, CSF Glucose 64 mg/dL, CSF Protein 48 mg/dL. Brain MRI: Unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of high fever, severe generalized rigidity, confusion, and significantly elevated creatine kinase in a patient taking haloperidol confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
